docs.minHistorySamples: How many past samples a service needs before it is judged at all. Below this it is skipped rather than guessed at, so a service that just started does not alert on its first reading.
docs.zScoreAnomaly: How far from its own recent baseline a metric must move to count as anomalous, in noise-normalised standard deviations (a healthy series' normal extreme is about 3). Lower fires more often.
docs.zScoreHigh: Deviation at or above this is HIGH rather than MEDIUM.
docs.zScoreCritical: Deviation at or above this is CRITICAL.
docs.minDeltaPercent: Even a large z-score is ignored unless the metric moved this many percentage points from its baseline. Stops an idle service going from 0.05% to 2% CPU from raising an incident.
docs.absoluteHighPercent: A CPU or memory reading above this is HIGH no matter how calm the baseline is - a service pinned at 75% is worth seeing even if it has been there long enough to look normal.
docs.absoluteCriticalPercent: A reading above this is CRITICAL regardless of deviation.
docs.flatlineStdDev: Below this standard deviation the baseline counts as flat. Dividing by a near-zero deviation makes z-scores explode, so the flat case is judged on absolute movement instead.
docs.flatlineDeltaPercent: On a flat baseline, how many points a metric must jump to be anomalous. This is the rule that catches an idle service suddenly doing work.
docs.flatlineCriticalPercent: On a flat baseline, a value above this is CRITICAL rather than HIGH.
docs.criticalServicesForCritical: How many services must be critical at once before the whole incident is CRITICAL rather than HIGH.
docs.silenceSamples: A service that is normally busy (CPU or network) and shows no activity at all for this many samples in a row is treated as frozen. This is how a hung service is caught: it sends no errors, it just goes quiet.
docs.monitoringGapShare: If at least this share of a target's services go silent or vanish at the same moment, the mapper reports a monitoring outage (collector or SSH problem) instead of blaming services.
docs.explainAwayGamma: How strongly a broken dependency explains its callers' errors and slowness. 1 = fully; 0 = ignore the call graph and rank by how abnormal each service is.
docs.cascadeEdgeProbability: Assumed chance that a failure spreads across one call edge, used for the "at risk next" list. It ranks who to watch; it is not a calibrated probability.

offline.note: Offline evaluation on recorded runs with injected faults. detected = share of faults with an alarm naming a touched service; caughtAndNamed = detected and the true root ranked first; falseAlarmsPerHour = alarms with no fault active.
